Gardens are an essential part of Islamic culture, symbolizing beauty, peace, and reflection. In traditional Islamic art and literature, gardens are often mentioned as a place of tranquility and spiritual growth. Ruwaydah is a reminder of the connection between the natural world and the Divine, the importance of nurturing and tending to these gifts from Allah, and the promise of paradise as a beautiful and nurturing garden.

The name Ruwaydah can also be seen as a reminder of the promise of paradise, where all creation will be nurtured and cherished, and where we will be able to enjoy the fruits of our labor and the abundance of Allah's blessings. Ruwaydah serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things in the universe and the importance of our role in preserving and protecting the natural world as a sacred trust from Allah.
